title: Local dimension at a group identity equals global dimension
statement: Let $k$ be any field and $G$ a group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type over $k$. Let $e\in G$ be the image of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ under its identity section. Then $\dim\mathcal O_{G,e}=\dim G$, with local Krull dimension and the topological Krull dimension of $G$ in $\{-\infty,0,1,\ldots,\infty\}$. No reducedness, smoothness or characteristic assumption is required.

source.place: Dimension paragraph; sk-i-cartier third proof paragraph

proof.text: Extend k to its algebraic closure. The global dimension is preserved, affine locally, by dimension base change. Dimension at a point is preserved by field extension; at the rational identity and its lift both points are closed, so this agrees with local-ring dimension.

Over the algebraic closure every closed point is rational. Translation by it is an automorphism sending the identity to that point, inducing an isomorphism of local rings. All closed-point local dimensions are therefore equal.

Scheme dimension is the supremum of local dimensions. Each point specializes to a closed point, and local dimension cannot decrease upon specialization by the chain description. The supremum is thus the common closed-point value; the identity makes it nonempty. Descend using the equalities from the first step.
